paper.title: {elrint3d}: A Three-Dimensional Nonadaptive Automatic Cubature Routine Using a Sequence of Embedded Lattice Rules
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 37(3), Article 35 (2010); collected as ACM TOMS Algorithm 906
paper.url: https://netlib.org/toms/906.zip (ACM article not read; ACM pages return 403 from this host)

code.commit: netlib TOMS archive 906.zip (fetched by scout 2026-11-27 into a fresh /tmp directory; read with zipfile, not executed)
code.note: C++ sources in 906/C++/Src (elrint3d.cc and helpers, precomputed lattice coordinates). Driver test01.cc integrates a Gaussian over the unit cube with requested relative error 1e-12 and prints the value, the error flag, the estimated error and the number of function values. Shipped reference res1 is the oracle.

claim.location: Shipped reference output res1 in 906.zip (member 906/C++/Drivers/res1), produced by test01.cc. Claim value: Cubature = 0.88505988548101766 for the Gaussian integrand over [0,1]^3 at requested relative error 1e-12.

reference.sha256: not computed for the member; the value is quoted here and compared as a number

claim.metric: Cubature value printed by test01 (cout precision 17).
claim.paper_value: The paper's table is not read (ACM 403). The value is the shipped reference output res1, written by the authors' driver.

tolerance.basis: The driver's own estimated error is 1.69e-14, so the value is stable to about 1e-14 within one compiler. 1e-9 absolute (about 1.1e-9 relative) covers compiler and floating-point ordering differences; a wrong lattice rule or sequence shifts the value by orders more. Fixed now, before any run; not to be loosened after a run.

cost.data_size: None; the integrand is in the driver.
cost.data_licence: No data. Source is the public netlib TOMS collected-algorithms archive.

why: The driver runs the adaptive embedded lattice cubature on a non-trivial 3-D integrand and prints the value, so a rerun must compile and run the C++ library to reproduce it; the value is not a closed form.
